skos:Concept.skos:scopeNote: {"id": "0b38da9e-2d73-4466-be0f-e1c754ec150a", "value": "A room or office at a general practitioners' or veterinary practice, where patients or animals are seen and medicine dispensed."}

skos:ConceptScheme.dcterms:title: {"id": "905ef431-5acb-4d97-9ccd-02c5abc33bb0", "value": "FISH Thesaurus of Monument Types"}
skos:ConceptScheme.dcterms:description: {"id": "055b1401-0749-4674-9e0c-64c7325efcbd", "value": "Terminology relating to the built and buried heritage of the British Isles and used for recording sites, monuments, buildings and structures."}

skos:Concept.skos:scopeNote: {"id": "af312801-e06d-4d2d-b948-09e9b3344bb4", "value": "A surgery where patients who pay for medical treatments are seen and treated."}
{"id": "dfc46b94-9d87-4b25-9331-3ed343311b3a", "value": "A building, often close to a churchyard, used for the entertainment of poor people on their wedding day."}
{"id": "c7a63567-d756-4182-89b3-4bf3eba93144", "value": "House owned by the church, often used for meetings."}
{"id": "678e3e1c-2e74-4e50-bf6b-84f2658e6a1b", "value": "A market building, pre-19th century, incorporating other function rooms, eg. theatres, courtrooms, schoolrooms."}
{"id": "82fee2cf-c4c2-4409-a234-2b9c7af370da", "value": "A hall associated with a church, used for holding functions, meetings and for conducting parish business."}

{"id": "aad7600e-34fd-4a11-87a1-ecfa7a336ca4", "value": "A large building used for the transaction of the public business of a town, the holding of courts of justice, entertainments and other activities."}
{"id": "c332018b-a29e-48d4-8633-891114e27689", "value": "Traditionally, the hall of a crafts, trade, or merchants' guild. Nowadays, often used to describe a TOWN HALL."}
{"id": "41cb446f-f299-4706-ae6f-815c9ccc3322", "value": "A site which has produced evidence of in situ production of items derived from antler."}
{"id": "05305764-ab4a-4e82-9c88-eec5470e67bb", "value": "An excavation from which cobble stone is obtained."}
{"id": "e5558604-a202-487b-9ec6-2b3392b38a20", "value": "A large, \"bottle-shaped\", oven of brick construction used in the baking or firing of pottery."}
{"id": "7daa4224-02c5-40e8-9adb-83fd817acd6f", "value": "A type of pottery oven in which the air passes from the base of the kiln out through the top."}
{"id": "f950e776-6a09-4353-908d-aad8f23d4fd9", "value": "A type of updraught intermittent kiln of rectangular plan and battered sides, but with an open top."}
{"id": "aa033a43-cd24-4c69-93ab-4286baeade1e", "value": "A type of pottery kiln in which air rises up inside the oven to be forced back down and out through the base of the oven."}
{"id": "247b2f11-0bbf-4247-9a1b-08090cf3a4b9", "value": "An inn temporarily used for the performance of plays and other public entertainment."}
{"id": "f60710bb-b4f5-4a00-a444-f301711bca11", "value": "An area of land and associated buildings where vines are cultivated. The grapes produced are then used to make wine."}
{"id": "250e9215-020f-4e2d-abf7-2b1904b57b7d", "value": "Pasture to which animals were driven for grazing, with associated temporary huts for domestic or agricultural use."}

{"id": "ea5c87a1-35db-4dbe-8296-7d4244b86db5", "value": "A trench dug through topsoil in an arable field in order to extract underlying clay which was then spread on the field and ploughed in to improve soil fertility. Usually found in peaty soil areas such as the Lincolnshire and Cambridgeshire fenlands."}

{"id": "5a2dc0a4-1691-4654-b728-b593d41f9c38", "value": "Ditches interrupted by wide, regular causeways. Each section of ditch is about 30-40m long, and each causeway is 10-15m wide. In some cases, a network of fields has been created. Found mainly in the South East of England."}
{"id": "098bde8d-c845-4339-95ff-ea25645a913e", "value": "An earthen bank indicating the limit of a wood or coppice"}
{"id": "47a68323-842e-44c5-aaf3-3c98535bca03", "value": "A cultivated plantation of watercress, usually situated near springs or small running streams."}
{"id": "c705ccae-7f27-4fc6-9eed-562396b67f66", "value": "An enclosed piece of land adjoining a house."}
{"id": "2d5dddc4-2da9-48f6-b034-c5aa93dc5fa4", "value": "Areas used for potato-growing."}
{"id": "9779d5eb-c734-4330-85d6-c50eff1dae48", "value": "A dwelling-house with outbuildings and land assigned to its use."}

{"id": "f430f3b5-1777-41a3-951b-4fcf782136e1", "value": "An outlying farm or estate, usually belonging to a religious order or feudal lord. Specifically related to core buildings and structures associated with monastic land holding. Use specific term where known."}
{"id": "30cf758d-866d-461f-9d3e-a9848de553a5", "value": "An area of land, usually on a slope, which has been built up to provide a flat surface for the cultivation of crops."}
{"id": "59eec53d-f11f-4947-a2f8-0e64b5f7e6e4", "value": "A place where osiers (willows) are grown for basket-making."}
{"id": "66bb9609-9a6d-4f0a-b74f-14767ce12d6b", "value": "A piece of land used for the cultivation of hops."}
{"id": "5af8e7cd-c2b6-4521-9b98-ed998827f64e", "value": "A group or complex of fields which appear to form a coherent whole. Use more specific type where known."}
{"id": "64e98fcf-1c9e-4fcd-a015-4f7d39f972f7", "value": "An earthen bank indicating the limit of a plantation."}
{"id": "ad671b7e-797a-4f54-8c7f-5feeeb0cdb73", "value": "An area of cultivated, managed woodland producing wood which is used for a variety of purposes."}
{"id": "83e84f22-e36b-419a-9308-4af49f68f8f6", "value": "A group of planted trees or shrubs, generally of uniform age and of a single species."}

{"id": "1318d263-0835-4f1b-a639-deeed8918182", "value": "A large tract of land covered with trees and interspersed with open areas of land. Traditionally forests were owned by the monarchy and had their own laws."}
{"id": "e6f17f40-15f1-4cd3-8580-c28ac4fbad7c", "value": "An area of land consisting of the lord's demesne and of lands from whose holders he may exact certain fees, etc."}

{"id": "fccf6438-c7e3-4897-8397-36105229ec75", "value": "A term for a type of house, with varying definitions according to period. Roman villas were high-status and usually associated with a rural estate, whereas Georgian and later period villas were often semi-detached, town houses."}
{"id": "60fb002a-01ef-4be8-946a-d27d6ec402eb", "value": "A holding on a smaller-scale than an ordinary farm."}
{"id": "a4aef5f1-4d10-4216-88e3-b921faa34d5d", "value": "A low lying area of land that is usually waterlogged at all times and is flooded in wet weather."}
{"id": "0c647988-6ebc-4791-85a0-8fcdcc5d3341", "value": "A plot of land longer than it is wide, can include any structures on it. Typical of medieval towns."}
{"id": "a764e6b1-a5c0-4428-b8cd-f33d69116665", "value": "A horticultural site where trees, shrubs and plants are grown for sale and transplanting elsewhere."}

{"id": "64d2acef-e88f-428b-bda1-dd5fe99d1b19", "value": "A small narrow rectilinear enclosure with high hedges boundaries for the cultivation and shelter of flowers, particularly Daffodils and Narcissi."}

{"id": "f04b0611-fe0e-4b72-8616-8567437a45da", "value": "A tract of land, often including a farmhouse and ancillary buildings, used for the purpose of cultivation and the rearing of livestock, etc. Use more specific type where known."}
{"id": "be8f38c9-70d3-485f-b5c2-43741c25606a", "value": "Areas of land used primarily for agriculture. See also GARDENS, PARKS AND URBAN SPACES."}
{"id": "2579faa0-dd83-4b4f-a113-12d00127892d", "value": "An area of land, often enclosed, used for cultivation or the grazing of livestock."}
{"id": "f6b62d91-623c-4135-a75b-ba8843edbd94", "value": "An area of ground which has been cleared of plants and other obstruction."}
{"id": "c6b78da4-ed70-4e7d-8a6e-9f805d5af2fa", "value": "A piece of grassland, often near a river, permanently covered with grass which is mown for use as hay."}
{"id": "7f7f1636-87ef-487a-ae7b-145d7c87f0a6", "value": "A piece of land used to grow vegetables to be sold at markets."}
{"id": "2a7cb102-d225-4e93-b19a-d01aef835a27", "value": "A share or portion of land, allotted to a person, often used for growing, vegetables, fruit, etc."}
{"id": "2cb11440-525b-4d80-bcce-b277284e7976", "value": "Unenclosed wasteland, forest and pasture used in common by the community."}
{"id": "d389191f-5f89-430c-8412-8c4271aa8ce9", "value": "A covered gateway, at the entrance to a churchyard, where during a funeral a coffin could be set down until the vicar arrived."}
{"id": "be6801ec-cfe0-48fb-91a1-eddca8fde0a4", "value": "A structure, often within a CHURCHYARD or LYCH GATE, on which a coffin could rest prior to burial."}
{"id": "ec9c399a-0b61-4a56-9799-5650b98f5dca", "value": "A road, used traditionally for the transportation of a corpse to a place of burial."}
{"id": "d38bc4f1-4076-4e64-b28f-ccf1056a4937", "value": "A stone found on route to a churchyard on which the coffin is rested during transportation."}
{"id": "de250318-d542-4f1a-a4e9-de292e61ecd8", "value": "A place, where a corpse could be laid whilst being carried on its way to a burial, to allow the bearers to rest."}
{"id": "d46f1be6-1e46-4767-8199-06073b29a8b4", "value": "A conduit or pipes, used primarily for conveying petroleum from oil wells to a refinery, or for supplying water to a town or district, etc."}

{"id": "87183dea-7e2d-4863-9139-e30a46680f90", "value": "A site associated with Operation PLUTO (Pipe Line Under The Ocean) the operation to supply the allies with fuel following the invasion of Normandy."}
{"id": "2cc5c1f9-eb95-4278-9886-fb37de706834", "value": "A bridge used for carrying liquids, usually water, although sometimes oil, in a pipeline over a river. Mid 19th century onwards."}
{"id": "1f25e1fc-98a4-48cc-bb3f-685754384877", "value": "A place of worship specifically for mariners and their families."}
{"id": "a28bc292-258d-4154-943e-e9f54c221157", "value": "Factory for the production of safety fuses used in the ignition of gunpowder for blasting."}
{"id": "f8ceea5f-03a2-45b6-946e-8c53a5f74104", "value": "An area within a hospital where children are accommodated during the period of their medical or surgical treatment."}
{"id": "a7e5270c-ddfc-4f92-b024-9b2c008fcbcd", "value": "A specialist hospital for the medical and surgical treatment of children."}

{"id": "df71ffec-343a-41fb-8928-56a3f8e4285f", "value": "A single-span aircraft hangar designed by Boulton & Paul of London and Norwich (drawing number 4178/44). Mainly used on aircraft factory sites and at Armament Training Schools."}

{"id": "f3502e56-f1f7-475b-86c6-43fc4a5e87b3", "value": "A type of aircraft hangar from the closing years of WWI either of steel or wood utilising a type of lattice work roof support known as a Belfast Truss, which features diagonally interlaced pieces of thin pine. The roof appears as a smooth curve."}

{"id": "f5b99d60-3d10-477d-8073-164d6b28abed", "value": "A permanent military RAF aircraft hangar type, designed in 1924. It features a steel frame (with longitudinal ridge and valley trusses for the roof) reinforced concrete and brick infilling for the walls. Typically 122 foot span by 249 foot in length."}

{"id": "928ad467-7b70-441a-90c5-a59da32118ea", "value": "A type of large steel framed aircraft hangar introduced by the Royal Air Force in its Expansion Period with a number of designs between 1934 and 1939, to accomodate heavy bombers."}
{"id": "02ecd3aa-3c0e-4bed-9c5f-98e1112d5227", "value": "1st World War end-opening aeroplane hangar."}
{"id": "2340372d-ef11-484a-a939-cd898b7403ef", "value": "A semi-permanent ahed designed to Air Ministry specification 1136/27 as a quick and cheap hangar for stations overseas"}
{"id": "2ce1644b-eee7-4305-a2ea-8ad64bda0654", "value": "1st World War end-opening aeroplane hangar."}
{"id": "9475d1ea-45a4-41b4-8832-58bedcc28d11", "value": "1st World War end-opening aeroplane hangar."}

{"id": "3ba58f14-70e3-4f1e-90a8-2d0ec7b00c1f", "value": "A mutiple role hangar for aircraft and general storage, manufactured in the USA as a kit for on-site assembly during WWII and post-war. It comprises a steel box frame and a canvas covering."}

{"id": "2280c9f2-d034-4d69-a473-9ca163279893", "value": "A type of large permanent military aircraft hangar with a curved steel frame and storage annexes on its side used in World War II. It was intended for storage purposes on Aircraft Storage Unit stations."}
{"id": "771a52e4-490d-4c7b-bf97-314d8c6c48e5", "value": "A structure used for the housing and servicing of aircraft."}
{"id": "f4980f43-3940-4fb3-b1a0-23a4fc9bc59e", "value": "An aircraft hangar designed to house seaplanes."}

{"id": "7b7d25b6-fe2b-4b5b-9e92-3e336a92fba5", "value": "Aircraft hangars designed by T. Bedford Consulting Engineers to meet the requirement to repair damaged heavy bombers in situ on their airfields."}
{"id": "f3c1c177-1774-40db-af18-a7af518b9a89", "value": "A coupled timber built end-opening First World War aircraft hangar."}

{"id": "65ade62a-6978-4046-bbbf-8f7f0801cb9d", "value": "The earliest side-opening standard type of aircraft hangar designed in 1913 and used in WWI. Originally constructed from wooden trusses and struts, some examples have steel frames. It comprised a single or coupled shed with rear workshops."}

{"id": "2ffa5daf-921c-4867-af04-82cdfdbf1c8d", "value": "A small dispersal WWII military aircraft hangar featuring an \"A\" shaped steel frame clad with corrugated iron; end doors were supported by outriggers when open.Typically used on aircraft storage units or satellite landing grounds. Variations in size."}
{"id": "85cb3727-25d4-4778-96bd-9a9810156832", "value": "A hangar used for the storage of barrage balloons."}

{"id": "0e20cdd0-1b65-452a-a374-a6ef735f6f25", "value": "An aircraft hangar designed to Air Ministry specification (drawing number 6910/43). Similar in design to the ROBINS AIRCRAFT HANGAR but larger."}

{"id": "f0bf922a-e56a-4f30-b682-af437b1b3ee4", "value": "An aircraft hangar designed to Air Ministry specifications (drawing number 2243/41). Constructed from prefabricated A-frames and clad in corrugated iron."}

{"id": "52e0d88a-e342-42e5-9294-fba1916c6b15", "value": "A military storage aircraft hangar built in the late 1930s. It comprises a semicircular concrete structure with reinforced concrete columns, featuring a curved roof and straight walls."}

{"id": "235bc30f-a611-4569-b435-fa03a7fb053d", "value": "A steel aircraft hangar evolved from the German \"Lamellendach\", a segmental roof design of the 1920s using a diamond shaped web of pressed steel producing a hangar with a shallow curving profile. Used for both military and civil purposes."}
{"id": "2afa7fe8-7e97-456c-a916-678f90bfca09", "value": "An aircraft hangar designed to be moved from site to site as necessary."}

{"id": "acbef6f1-97e5-4ebd-8f8f-6c6e9d5002ae", "value": "A curved military aircraft hangar produced in 1939. The frame is steel which is then clad with steel sheeting and reinforced concrete and typically covered with a thin layer of concrete, earth and turf."}
{"id": "d0b73213-3fb2-4c44-800d-ebc70cac0588", "value": "1st World War end-opening aeroplane hangar."}

{"id": "38fed7f1-2c04-4707-8658-3dd4d0cb19cf", "value": "A double-span aircraft hangar designed by Boulton & Paul of London and Norwich. Mainly used on aircraft factory sites and at Armament Training Schools."}

{"id": "68347bde-5b6f-48ec-8dbf-68bd4dbfd26f", "value": "A large steelframed military aircraft hangar designed in 1939, intended for aircraft maintenance on operational stations. It includes side annexes for workshops and offices, provided with a large number of windows. The annexes are of brick or concrete."}

{"id": "515c8811-aad4-4a5e-90db-b67b6bc6f45d", "value": "A military storage aircraft hangar designed in 1937. It has a curved profile and is constructed from steel ribs supporting a concrete skin. The roof is covered with earth and turf."}
{"id": "90592042-74c8-48ae-96d7-df0e66f02a2c", "value": "A shed used for the maintenance and repair of aircraft."}

{"id": "3f0ad9ac-5f67-4697-b3fe-c6d75fe1500d", "value": "A type of military aircraft hangar of the Cold War, hardened and therefore protected against the effects of nuclear weapons. It comprises a semi-circular structure built of corrugated-steel supporting a reinforced-concrete skin. Three NATO designs."}
{"id": "243e9616-9522-4482-a367-50aacebcc953", "value": "A house with a pitched roof with a double slope and gables on the front and rear elevations of the building."}
{"id": "a44cac09-7ebf-4bc9-8fce-8c0da1b50fae", "value": "A house with a pitched or gabled roof with a double slope and gables on two or more sides."}
{"id": "84b7f065-e68b-4e02-8e08-8f4bfb448e75", "value": "A house with a pitched roof with a double slope and gables on the side elevations of the building."}
{"id": "8a55c39f-7dd4-4ae7-b17d-d3b145e56df8", "value": "A building used to dry flax."}
{"id": "e3521d53-4c1f-4a6a-9693-18858231e96f", "value": "Posts with hooks attached to allow drying new cloth to be stretched out between them."}
{"id": "41543b8e-0950-4cb4-ad54-552687d1fdd1", "value": "Large wooden hammer beams pounding cloth in a fulling solution."}
{"id": "920f6eae-371b-40e6-99b8-21243daee765", "value": "A building or structure in which processed cloth is dried."}
{"id": "aa81e801-40ff-4275-8786-ecdf7aca531c", "value": "A type of clothier's house, consisting of TOPSHOP and dwelling, used for hand-weaving of textiles."}
{"id": "89fda212-ff80-4b9d-b137-22a3b131619e", "value": "A workshop containing machinery used to press textiles."}
{"id": "7d5307c1-4e8f-46f3-a971-b75504d29571", "value": "Large field or yard used to lay fabrics out ready for bleaching."}
{"id": "7f00e197-f65f-46e8-80f8-0dc32ab56920", "value": "A heated room or building used to dry yarn after it has been washed."}
{"id": "fad45a27-8dd3-4cc8-a3a6-0a21eb3ec50b", "value": "A structure used for drying yarn in open fields."}
{"id": "20cc170a-db58-4eb3-9dc0-e152b1935b62", "value": "A stone on which flax stems were beaten with wooden mallets, a process known as beetling."}
{"id": "72f4bf30-59e0-491c-a9f9-4ccc6ef509f7", "value": "A building used to dry wool in."}
{"id": "4940a5f1-ae61-4c8f-8af8-0dd499d665fb", "value": "Field or area of ground where washed new cloth is stretched out to dry."}
{"id": "cf8492af-6db6-4eee-bdce-15bdf01424a6", "value": "A building used for drilling out the bores of cannon and other military pieces."}
{"id": "cf6f0845-2492-4629-a565-2a81c5ecc639", "value": "A building containing a machine tool for boring out large cylindrical holes in items such as steam engine cylinders, pump barrels, etc."}
{"id": "26dc2baa-cb26-455b-82ca-28377d1207d9", "value": "An area of land, roughly shaped like a polygon and enclosed by a boundary ditch, bank, wall, palisade or similar barrier."}

{"id": "5de7c0ac-33fc-47ca-a01b-22d474c9ced1", "value": "Standard dwelling of the non-ruling classes of Japan until the mid twentieth century. Minkas are timber-framed houses with mud-plastered panels and thatched roofs. The design varies from region to region. Minkas served as home as well as workplace."}
{"id": "83559e26-92e7-4b22-b197-8c14eb388d04", "value": "Use where the intervening arcade is closed but timber-framed."}
{"id": "4d520d2c-af50-4dc4-a332-11aea13017f9", "value": "A house built using experimental building techniques and materials."}
{"id": "f9839683-54d2-4efb-afa6-848d8db4c2e8", "value": "A house provided for the treasurer of a cathedral, palace or similar."}
{"id": "b0faf327-30ac-4279-8adb-d46c05b80e00", "value": "The principal house of a manor or village."}
{"id": "d3410a93-5fbb-4aae-b05e-1af2295e508a", "value": "Cottage provided for guests to a country house."}
{"id": "7bd569d5-8e9d-41eb-abad-6ae15cdcd02b", "value": "A house joined to another to form one building."}
{"id": "f8048513-1331-4904-a3ef-488fd0c6097b", "value": "A small paved area attached to a building."}
{"id": "82234197-2d29-4fb7-b2fd-d0bb27a8891d", "value": "A house in a line of houses attached to and adjoining one another and planned and built as one unit."}
{"id": "b19754d4-20d4-4282-a388-41bfdc861d90", "value": "The residence of an engineer."}
{"id": "c8db3a51-091c-4cd2-af5d-b43a2ef41d2c", "value": "A purpose-built dwelling for the supervisor of a factory, mine or other industrial complex."}

{"id": "cb34c471-e231-4847-ae43-1c7a326075e0", "value": "An island, partly or wholly artificial, built up by dumping timber, earth and stones onto a lake or river bed. Often revetted with timber piles or palisade."}
{"id": "2b8bd01b-14a0-4030-af34-6d48be773ed1", "value": "A building providing lodgings for police constables."}
{"id": "37de220e-0eec-4af9-83b3-632751ca161b", "value": "The residence of a person employed in the textile industry."}
{"id": "ab979e15-be59-49f0-af8c-8c82a9d2481d", "value": "A dwelling house forming part of a Chartist Land Colony."}
{"id": "4db816b9-b12c-44c7-954a-a60baa8fd5a1", "value": "The residence of a well keeper."}

{"id": "3d5960dd-ab54-42bd-b0da-37b0ce5f3a71", "value": "A type of prefabricated house erected, to 11 approved designs, as part of the Temporary Housing Programme, between 1944 and 1948. This scheme was devised to relieve the post-war housing shortage at a time when conventional materials were unavailable."}

{"id": "04a86c1c-b709-48db-841d-3bc178c56631", "value": "Circular structure, normally indicated by one or more rings of post holes and/or a circular gulley, and usually interpreted as being of domestic function."}
{"id": "7fb5a8c9-6081-4c18-ac6c-135a889ac399", "value": "The residence of a telegraph keeper, associated with a telegraph station."}
{"id": "4c1333bd-becc-4006-aec7-4c9b7f55a922", "value": "A small yard attached to the rear of a house or other building."}
{"id": "78bd9a3f-4809-44e4-b4cd-c3cc8839bd54", "value": "The dwelling place of a farm worker."}
{"id": "9209edbf-ce60-4555-8181-7deb0704548f", "value": "The place where a house stood or had once stood, often adjoining a garth or croft."}
{"id": "ecb21fa5-4a66-4763-aaae-2ce0f6f82b4d", "value": "The residence of a person entrusted with the management of a great house or castle."}
{"id": "230b7606-b56e-44b8-b3ea-8c0ef15d0b56", "value": "A forester's cottage."}
{"id": "3e129f0b-dec9-4b1b-9c74-85b59f5b0bcd", "value": "A house consisting of a public hall with private living accommodation attached. Built from the medieval period onwards."}
{"id": "9e265ee2-8136-4280-8a9b-a0c7262b018a", "value": "A one-storey house."}
{"id": "1f60c7f6-1933-4f90-8ca5-42d97dcd403c", "value": "A Swiss-styled house, usually with steeply pitched and projecting roof."}

{"id": "5cc12f0a-959a-4c6f-b1aa-a94430f8ec0f", "value": "A house, the inhabitant of which keeps an official register e.g. a registrar's house near a cemetery would keep an official record of deaths and burials."}

{"id": "bf3c6d63-be22-4906-86e9-3a06c305e95b", "value": "A step or ramp in the bank of a canal to enable horses to climb out of the water."}

{"id": "3c090548-bd66-4de4-9547-12c903ad0ff8", "value": "Use with other minerals extracted and MINE where relevant, eg. ZINC MINE."}

{"id": "7c8b1fbb-d409-4e80-b74b-96fcc2817935", "value": "A mine used for the extraction of any hard dark-coloured rock."}

{"id": "9927d314-cf1e-4424-a26a-a890b1dd9a05", "value": "A control tower constructed on RNAS stations by the Royal Marine Engineers. Built to a common ground floor plan they could be built with one, two or three storeys above this depending on the requirements of the station."}
{"id": "f68177ec-c61d-494e-bca3-1c45bd7747eb", "value": "A small detached building used to accommodate patients with tuberculosis."}
{"id": "42001cd3-1c31-4c40-8675-31cc1a49f1e4", "value": "A hospital for convalescents or consumptives."}

{"id": "77b59473-132b-4065-a895-5b39fe7ac00c", "value": "An oval or circular structure with seats rising in tiers around a central open space. Used for religious ceremonies, entertainment, training and armed combat contests."}
{"id": "fde718ee-af30-4ddf-a88f-e9cad4775109", "value": "Use only for a monastic house of unknown status, religious order and uncertain authenticity."}
{"id": "1d9c196e-1a05-41c9-8f3c-7bf4334581df", "value": "A large bath used for Jewish ritual ceremonies."}
{"id": "b0f35d3f-1cb0-46cf-857a-2436df06ba8a", "value": "Site types normally or frequently associated with burials which in some instances may have had solely religious or ritual functions."}
{"id": "fd48c10e-7093-4948-ab5e-2ef88c9381d8", "value": "Underground chambers and stone passages of Iron Age date found in South West England."}

{"id": "52a89773-f6c6-4493-a827-f21d75a5ce9f", "value": "A tall, polygonal structure with ornamental roofs at each storey which is associated with Buddhist temples; the style was adapted for secular eyecatchers and pavilions in the 18th century in England."}

{"id": "e84c3c5e-101c-4f30-bf72-4149c58c4068", "value": "A building containing a series of seats for use by the clergy during services. The seats are usually placed in the church and as such this is a very rare monument type, being purpose-built. An example being St. Germoe's Chair in Germoe, Cornwall."}

{"id": "7a43f9f2-89f2-44d4-9ba8-43e1ffbaaecb", "value": "Prehistoric structure consisting of three or more standing stones in close proximity to each other, forming an unroofed approximately rectangular structure open in one direction."}
{"id": "cb1867cc-2a6a-4366-af5f-422044dd3cdf", "value": "Material, stone or wood, lining the inside of a grave."}
{"id": "c63a0195-a6f8-48c4-a41b-b8bf2672c179", "value": "A vessel to contain holy water located near the entrance of a church."}
{"id": "aa5ad5d4-b91b-4d39-a74c-903f5463b5db", "value": "A cleansing house associated with Jewish burial ceremonies"}

{"id": "fe9cc580-1d57-4859-89dc-ae37185af075", "value": "An arrangement of one or more standing stones. Use particularly for isolated recumbent stones, or where original form of monument unclear. Use specific type where known."}
{"id": "854ce7c5-3c86-4416-818a-892c6e41796e", "value": "A building used as a meeting place by a synod, an assembly of the clergy."}
{"id": "698435db-47f6-47f0-b9a6-d3e2d3cb83cd", "value": "Prayer hall at burial ground, especially a small walk-in memorial devoted to a deceased Hasidic rabbi."}

{"id": "abdf01ca-2dac-479f-b9d1-8edfff67c751", "value": "A covered walk, walled on one side and usually arcaded on the other, surrounding or partly surrounding an open area in a monastery or similar complex of Christian buildings."}

{"id": "657ac6d7-e52a-4081-8692-c4303519ca32", "value": "A free-standing structure, in the form of a cross (+), symbolizing the structure on which Jesus Christ was crucified and sacred to the Christian faith. Use specific type where known."}

{"id": "ad27ace0-272b-4396-8c7a-da46cae4d032", "value": "A circular bank of stones and turf, sometimes accompanied by a ditch, surrounding a natural outcrop of rock, usually a tor, or an earthfast boulder."}

{"id": "03ebc41d-e41b-4301-9972-7de2d204eb9a", "value": "A perforated stone basin usually built into the wall of a church on the south side of the altar. Used for carrying away the ablutions (wine and water used to rinse the chalice, and wash the priests hands after communion)."}

{"id": "5e7d7056-6ad1-4e05-899f-de9e6222df9a", "value": "A well or spring, possessing religious or otherwise ritualistic significance, around which a structure, such as a niche, wall or shelter, has been constructed. In the case of the water source being a natural spring, double-index with SPRING."}

{"id": "377a83a3-980f-4d97-a30f-27c563ecdcbc", "value": "The building attached to a cathedral or collegiate church where the dean, prebendaries or monks and canons met for the transaction of business."}

{"id": "c59811d8-bba2-401c-99eb-1b228563a5b1", "value": "A pit which appears to have been dug for, or which contains, objects apparently deposited for reasons other than storage, disposal or extraction. Index with principal object types."}
{"id": "99e7e727-19d5-4da7-a13d-e4e7236d6bb0", "value": "An enclosure surrounded by a wooden stockade. A rare site type of Neolithic date."}
{"id": "305c30e6-5cde-4246-b498-ffc79ee66007", "value": "A room or part of a church where the vestments, vessels and records are kept."}
{"id": "797ff64f-4ed3-4266-a683-7e32cd5ab816", "value": "A stone on which a monarch traditionally sat during the coronation ceremony."}
{"id": "f768fde8-25be-449e-9b6a-c4145d7a2727", "value": "A communal residence of secular priests and/or other clerics sometimes with the condition of learning and education attached."}
{"id": "93a62f97-d506-47ae-aa18-1d7c398b65c4", "value": "A place where worship is offered or devotions are paid to a deity or saint."}
{"id": "c27545ea-5274-423e-a9ff-4ee8ba1efd93", "value": "A single line, or two or more roughly parallel lines, of standing stones set at intervals along a common axis or series of axes."}

{"id": "196c3962-ae5f-497e-bb10-1a308158a8c4", "value": "A confusing and baffling network of winding and intercommunicating paths, often bordered by high hedges or walls. Some early examples are believed to have had ritual uses. Use more specific type where known."}
{"id": "172f36aa-dc9a-43a6-abef-873246cfcbbf", "value": "A giant figure of a man, animal or symbol carved on chalk hillsides mainly in southern England."}
{"id": "d1cca06f-433f-4e23-91e1-cbdb8ddfd318", "value": "A space in a Buddist building that is used for teaching Dharma/Dhamma - the teachings of Buddha."}
{"id": "6c9e54d3-e5e9-4362-a1e2-4e6b25e8c148", "value": "Refers to art, whether carving or painting, applied to free -standing stones or cave walls."}

{"id": "e28638e3-7eec-47f2-a419-217b2eeb6e07", "value": "A monument within a church or cathedral representing one of the stations of the cross. Usually images or pictures of successive incidents of the Passion, they are intended to be visited for meditation and prayer."}

{"id": "9c118346-06cd-496a-a2b2-40593108a1af", "value": "Approximately circular or oval setting of spaced post holes indicating the former presence of a free-standing arrangement of upright timber posts. Often regarded as a wooden equivalent of the better known stone circles."}
{"id": "4976576f-ce68-4ddf-81c6-41c0ee8121af", "value": "A vessel, usually made of stone, which contains the consecrated water for baptism. Use a broader monument type if possible."}

{"id": "d7e17cf9-2dbe-4e52-811f-4057e5b21959", "value": "A monument comprising an irregularly circular enclosing ditch, interrupted by several causeways, surrounding a central circular area used for funerary activities, often concealed originally beneath an earthen mound. Index with barrow type where known."}

{"id": "eeaecbb8-91e2-4644-beba-13a2f3dd587f", "value": "An enclosure of Late Neolithic/Early Bronze Age date, related to henges, defined by a circular arrangement of pits, probably none of which originally held posts. More than one circle, concentrically arranged, may be present."}
{"id": "522604fd-6eab-488c-ae9c-3ba195d49a97", "value": "A Prehistoric monument type in South West England in which a natural boulder is surrounded by a man-made kerb of stones."}

{"id": "2e79ae8f-7c50-4384-a657-0b5ffb07e96d", "value": "Circular or sub-circular enclosure defined by a bank and (usually internal) ditch, with one or two (rarely more) entrances. Of ceremonial/ritual function, they contain a variety of internal features including timber or stone circles."}

{"id": "e3801c52-90df-424b-a368-ce3e69adda1a", "value": "A shaft which appears to have been dug for, or which contains objects apparently deposited for, reasons other than storage, disposal or extraction (eg. of stone, water, etc). Index with principal object types."}

{"id": "6ad9329e-0448-4a41-9062-8e7f5d6a5eab", "value": "An approximately circular or oval setting of spaced, usually freestanding, upright stones. More than one circle may be present, arranged concentrically."}
{"id": "cf87dd40-7887-4766-acb5-fc9aa66ae7d2", "value": "A stone on which Runes have been inscribed. Often used as memorials though not always associated with a burial."}

{"id": "afb01b5e-8a7c-4ea0-a711-ec59ec00f0df", "value": "The area surrounding a monastic house including conventual buildings, outbuildings, cemetery, fishponds, etc, usually marked out by a bank and/or ditch or precinct wall."}
{"id": "08f4f92a-bbb6-4a1d-ad26-779843531b1a", "value": "A Cornish Medieval amphitheatre used for the performance of mystery plays and sports."}
{"id": "3b586676-ca26-4b5f-b731-b0d672467b9c", "value": "A rectilinear ritual enclosure of Iron Age date"}
{"id": "e4a8f35c-fe15-477f-ac92-cc2c1c0e0485", "value": "An area of a church, often a free-standing building, in which baptism is administered"}
{"id": "292565e2-13d9-4ec7-8ecd-173772be23b3", "value": "An elevated table or podium on which to place or sacrifice offerings to the deities."}

{"id": "7c2fd1f4-342f-4f29-ac0f-22c96485e2dd", "value": "A single line, or pair of roughly parallel lines, of pits set at intervals along a common axis or series of axes. The pits are not thought to have held posts."}
{"id": "8323ec97-d0d9-4090-8cb2-0edbf4b30f3b", "value": "A shelter for the parson during the burial service."}
{"id": "20059199-f827-4520-b72a-ad2d76813c8b", "value": "An establishment providing medical or surgical treatment for the ill or wounded. Use narrower term where possible."}
{"id": "ad28a3a8-9253-4511-b91a-4e04992526f0", "value": "A place for keeping vestments and sacred vessels."}
{"id": "c2b0bb3c-9b89-41e4-a400-ac724d551d3a", "value": "A dedicated room for housing the organ feeder bellows, can be an underground chamber or a free-standing building."}
{"id": "7964069c-9243-4313-a98c-6d0b5fdd19ec", "value": "A building containing a bier; a movable stand on which a corpse, often in a coffin, is placed prior to burial."}
{"id": "3e206c15-2e24-4b8e-a3ad-ddc22838f40d", "value": "An office which administers the affairs of the church."}
{"id": "73796912-f7d8-4968-a596-279d2bfdb29e", "value": "A building used for meetings and worship by a religious community trying to propogate its faith in an area."}
{"id": "439d4178-fa67-4fd4-b52c-0baf5f2444cd", "value": "A house devoted to the shelter of the poor and endowed by a benefactor for this use."}
{"id": "d5cdde98-5914-4085-879c-2e0399e9d290", "value": "A covered way or passage especially in a cathedral or monastic church, leading east from the cloisters between transept and chapter house."}

{"id": "5a2b19a4-3969-4ffb-a595-f218cec4e22c", "value": "An early Medieval commemorative monument in the form of a stone which has been inscribed with symbols."}
{"id": "9f5e8b37-51d0-4cd4-9de5-a09f4a60a10c", "value": "A room used for the ritual cleaning of the body prior to burial"}

{"id": "986b6947-a827-4e13-b003-8df12e3f543f", "value": "A house or centre used for meditation, contemplation and/or prayer."}
{"id": "8f5aadd3-60ac-4a54-960d-d1120de55920", "value": "Upright stones engraved on the edges with a Celtic script consisting of lines or notches."}
{"id": "34cc1c22-fa27-4cfd-abfd-6aac73be6a18", "value": "A sacred area of a building or a consecrated piece of land."}
{"id": "1f35f369-3be2-4380-9c63-b0c90216111c", "value": "A tower or turret in which bells are hung."}
{"id": "3c4bf4a1-c5aa-45b6-865a-2594788fc396", "value": "A place of meeting and worship for followers of the Church Army, a body of trained lay evangelists devoted to evangelism and social work."}

{"id": "e466e390-345c-4981-930a-9ca1035a7985", "value": "A hiding place for a (Roman Catholic) priest."}
{"id": "7a1c95ce-6420-45fb-ba24-a1e17aa29553", "value": "A stone with a cross carved into the surface."}
{"id": "c0c1466e-9ec8-4036-9ca0-d1d52f031796", "value": "The open space surrounded by a cloister."}

Includes ancillary buildings, structures & features of uncertain use, which are thought to be \u00ef\u00bf\u00bdritual\u00ef\u00bf\u00bd (eg. hill figures)."}
{"id": "580066c8-72bc-4130-bf48-874326a905b7", "value": "A stone or boulder which lies lengthways on the ground and may be used as a table, altar etc. Use only for isolated stones."}

{"id": "1c4e6bd3-351c-46b1-bbe8-a0911835de10", "value": "A representation of the crucifixion of Christ or related scenes as a sculpture in a churchyard, etc."}

{"id": "6aaa212e-ecd1-47bf-8e8a-4865635462d2", "value": "A stone or boulder which has been deliberately set upright in the ground. Use only for isolated stones. Otherwise use specific type where known."}
{"id": "47b20475-8f21-495e-972f-08894f603154", "value": "A separate residence for guests, a house on a private estate or a monastery building specifically for receiving visitors."}

{"id": "4ac83368-e400-4b7b-b181-1bf64eea127a", "value": "A small hut, dwelling or cave, usually in a secluded spot, in which a hermit lived. Hermits chose to live solitary lives often due to religious motives."}

{"id": "1e8542e7-4ee1-4a83-b20b-647e21a32784", "value": "Religious establishment, founded in Somerset, where free love was practised."}
{"id": "0e904e80-56d4-4044-8b75-9149ee0b128e", "value": "A threshing barn which also houses farm animals and is somethimes used to stotre grain, house carts and other functions."}

{"id": "2994267c-98d5-4f32-9816-334e6e658219", "value": "A loft over a stable or barn used for storing hay."}

{"id": "bd09c2e7-8226-4555-8411-944bd78b1e86", "value": "A two storied open fronted structure comprising a cattle or cart shelter on the ground floor with a hayloft above. Most common in South West England."}

{"id": "0c80fc21-7390-454c-8e93-7a9eadd8dfd2", "value": "An isolated barn, cow house or shelter shed with a hayloft. Typically found in areas where farmsteads and fields were sited at a long distance from each other."}
{"id": "fd18903a-60f4-4d7e-95ac-9f56a04c21dd", "value": "A building used as a temporary form of accommodation during a holiday, which includes self-catering."}
{"id": "13411de4-6828-4bfb-b1cf-df6fe3544668", "value": "A place where (young) holiday-makers and hikers can be put up cheaply for the night."}

{"id": "e45eaab2-57c0-4e25-bb23-80ef59569784", "value": "A natural spring located within a, usually small, man-made structure, such as a niche or a box. The structure is so placed to accomodate use for a specific non-religious function, such as communal bathing."}

{"id": "fc5305f7-13c5-471e-93ec-41a9538df6f2", "value": "A building in which the ingredients of an explosive charge are weighed into their correct proportions and mixed prior to incorporation."}
{"id": "bc4a49c8-54fe-4091-b2ae-1d1fb8af5c25", "value": "A public house offering lodgings to the passengers, and stabling for the horses of stage coaches."}
{"id": "8c7422ba-87e9-4b8b-ab58-330d32d26048", "value": "An outbuilding where a horse-drawn carriage is kept."}
{"id": "7fc0950f-488f-4c0f-a40b-36c2cdf18360", "value": "A stable where horses are kept at livery, or are let out for hire."}
{"id": "b30a2f56-32e9-44d4-9f07-b92280ec8e06", "value": "A building, similar to a cart shed, but used to house traps, gigs and coaches."}
{"id": "62d166f8-d4dd-4a38-9bd6-12c9c0041396", "value": "An outbuilding used for the storage and maintenance of horse-drawn carriages."}
{"id": "fa58849f-2746-46d3-ad58-6a84d0326565", "value": "A building in which horses are accommodated."}
{"id": "b62d3ad6-9303-420c-a293-f5250c343d01", "value": "A stable used for riding horses or those used to pull coaches, gigs, etc."}
{"id": "7b6c0e23-f984-40d0-9546-4a86f5536487", "value": "The residence of a coachman."}
{"id": "eeb81646-e20d-4012-95d5-5b046202a5cc", "value": "A stable found at a coaching inn where horses are housed."}
{"id": "d9695435-b1c6-4272-9c39-4190e07a2b6e", "value": "A natural flow or current of water issuing from a source."}
{"id": "3a0aa103-e491-4267-a579-f6908714d026", "value": "A settlement where previous house sites are now unoccupied, but often visible as earthworks, crop or soil marks."}

{"id": "f7b89b4b-274f-43fc-809e-8fd98ad6a502", "value": "A works where bleach is manufactured."}
{"id": "567b9f65-cac9-42b1-977c-69be6edcff3b", "value": "A coke-filled tower used for the dissolving and neutralising of acid produced by alkali-making processes."}
{"id": "52c863ef-c8bb-490d-b4de-335cf2cc980a", "value": "A kiln used for the production of any of the soda group of alkalis by the heating of plant remains or salt."}

{"id": "d557231d-5ff5-458f-a11b-68bd563c1991", "value": "A site used for the production of sodium bicarbonate, soda ash or caustic soda."}
{"id": "fd3ce549-9673-4745-bdc3-1f9c53e6814b", "value": "A grave lined with slabs of stone or slate and covered by a large slab of stone. Commonly found on the Isle of Man."}
{"id": "87fd841f-40f7-4f97-a493-c31a570d6b93", "value": "A cemetery comprising inhumations or cremations interred in stone cists."}

Designed by the British Concrete Federation during WWII to be resistant to bomb blasts & used for military accommodation, child nurseries and clinics etc."}

{"id": "7a29717d-ada2-4f60-a7b1-574ffa659bd3", "value": "Special concrete loading ramps nicknamed 'hards' had been constructed along river banks, beaches and inlets to enable organised embarkation onto various types of landing craft to take place, irrespective of tides."}
{"id": "8aed971c-526a-4c13-894f-05694a03c8ad", "value": "Permanently moored historic maritime craft preserved and converted into a museum and open to the public."}
{"id": "21ffd767-1e2a-42dc-98df-951684eb7e0a", "value": "The remains of a vessel which has either sunk or suffered structural damage to the extent where it can no longer function."}
{"id": "232c9a48-4c80-444f-a86d-02a0f654c14c", "value": "A carving, often a bust or full-length figure, originally found above a ship's cutwater. Use as an external feature only."}
{"id": "0cc28c8b-08ac-44a2-8e91-e1c96518ff12", "value": "Buildings, sites and structures associated with the construction and repair of ships and boats."}
{"id": "8edadfec-56ed-420f-ae35-2191b9f39224", "value": "A place where vessels can land passengers and goods."}

{"id": "7d3f5e0e-cc0f-4e66-bb0e-63e887dcc09e", "value": "Hut along the coast, which provided shelter for lookouts known as \"huers\", who kept watch for the pilchard shoals that passed by the coast. Built of stone or wood. Particular common to Cornwall."}

{"id": "dc66e964-ffd9-433d-bb6c-bbc1e1537c12", "value": "Area or zone of sea where a battle, skirmish or action was fought between naval ships or warships and privateers. Not to be used for enemy action upon mercantile ships or a sudden strike by mine/torpedo against an enemy warship."}
{"id": "bc9180f0-09cb-4062-83a3-da8146b4fb26", "value": "Buildings, sites and structures used by mariners for purposes of navigation."}
{"id": "9612e490-6969-4415-a729-566658335746", "value": "Buildings, sites and structures associated with the defence of the coastline from foreign invasion."}
{"id": "5b8984e0-0a7a-4689-8caa-90e52b725e47", "value": "An unidentified feature on the seabed recorded by fishermen as an obstruction to trawling."}
{"id": "7a815260-31ec-4bb4-afbc-99b90a0ca04e", "value": "A building used by labourers who clean and pump the docks, and in general, assist shipwrights."}
{"id": "3d2d6430-313a-4fa7-a819-9fadd9d5cc6c", "value": "The rigging mast of a sailing ship erected as a monument. Used for naval displays."}
{"id": "cdd1be2e-a022-4af0-b638-67e556d5a972", "value": "An artificial mound created by the disposal of aggregate originally used as ballast in ships."}
{"id": "b81a6fe0-b91b-4087-ab8d-902edb333d0d", "value": "A scientific laboratory where marine life is studied and researched."}
{"id": "23fd54e0-73be-4ecc-b800-c6e6bf44a282", "value": "An area off the coast where ships anchor."}
{"id": "a47def97-a4b8-47c3-b9d5-182adba023ee", "value": "A component of another building, often a house, used for storing nets."}

{"id": "d062f03f-c7d5-4ae8-a63a-da1604731b1c", "value": "A boat, ship or other vessel either whole or in part. Watercraft often survive as commemorative monuments or have been reused as floating restaurants, museums, hotels etc."}

{"id": "145e0fc9-e8d9-4ebd-a9c1-3442cf492c62", "value": "Sites, building, structures & features associated with the construction, maintenance & supply of maritime craft. Includes associated ancillary structures such as navigation aids, dockyards, wharves, etc; does not include vessels."}
{"id": "a4e8e1dd-d994-44bd-a867-d929be30edb8", "value": "Small vernacular building used by fishermen for the preparing of nets and storage of equipment."}
{"id": "a05a39a7-d011-4886-8945-a5dd78b14235", "value": "An area of the sea or coastline where vessels have been abandoned."}
{"id": "8bb793fe-4641-4f44-937a-d11986fb27ba", "value": "Buildings, structures and sites for regulating the flow of water."}
{"id": "195d747c-8e51-4f78-be28-462c55c46934", "value": "A site where the magnetic signature of ships was lowered thereby making them less susceptible to magnetic mines."}

{"id": "c6e53b34-696e-4578-9edd-0fbbfb3bad2c", "value": "Graves known to be of shipwreck victims buried close to their site of discovery, as was customary until the 19th century, rather than in consecrated ground."}

{"id": "e4898e1e-14fb-4858-9251-f58e3e3add14", "value": "A building, usually associated with a port or dock, where seamen could get a meal and a cheap room. Often established by religious groups for the moral betterment of seamen."}
{"id": "12b97daf-59f4-4f78-83bf-a71d081f9b98", "value": "A building for the storage of all stores supplied for naval service other than victualling and armament."}
{"id": "695d487e-0ac1-425f-a9dc-3c1aa2329c26", "value": "A complex of buildings with the purpose of providing and storing food and drink supplies (esp. for the navy)."}
{"id": "d22d84be-ef3d-4cac-ad11-56f91c07053f", "value": "A free-standing building with enough space to hang and dry nets."}
{"id": "dc0bfa2b-2346-48c8-a9b2-858190fb8790", "value": "Non-military maritime flood and erosion defences."}

{"id": "e9f9fb6d-b08a-489b-aa17-f135ffde769c", "value": "A human constructed underwater structure, usually built to promote marine life in areas with a generally featureless eas bed but have also been built to control erosion, block ship passage, or improve surfing."}
{"id": "7f63b1ae-e2da-46c6-bfe5-f69951f286bd", "value": "A commercial premises supplying ships with provisions."}
{"id": "fa8a73ad-b9c7-4e73-af80-33420018db57", "value": "A structure inclined towards the water on which a ship may be built or lowered into the water."}
{"id": "9fd0f78b-8934-4f38-92ff-e2105308fba9", "value": "A route across a river, or lake. Use only for small inland ferries and index with LANDING POINT/STAGE/STEPS or PIER where known."}
{"id": "64ba5dcb-29fc-4dc7-bc40-1c5947e1c23f", "value": "A building or site where the carcasses of whales were butchered and rendered into by products such as oil, fenk and whalebone."}

{"id": "9df8f703-82b9-4476-ba0e-f4be1a57a54e", "value": "Feature, typically a ship, boat, aircraft or vehicle, deliberately sunk for recreational and diver educational purposes in inland bodies of water used as dive centres, such as lakes and water-filled quarries, or offshore as artificial reefs."}
{"id": "122d3847-e7e6-4129-b9e6-32f39583cbf5", "value": "An area, often including a platform, used for boxing competitions."}
{"id": "d85d4581-c1b5-4362-835f-cfcd9f9eee07", "value": "A venue, with a boxing ring and associated facilities, which is used to train for and undertake amateur or professional boxing."}
{"id": "bc5c7042-10a9-4787-85df-8521cd6fa39f", "value": "A place where dead bodies are buried together. Often unconsecrated ground."}

{"id": "4b097baf-e9fd-41f2-aed3-c7bb002514be", "value": "A pit in which lye is used to clean hides/bones/etc. generally as part of the tanning process to remove excess fat, flesh, hair, etc. from the raw hide. The residue from these pits formed a crude soap which could be used for various cleaning purposes."}
{"id": "b3975b8e-da3a-400d-b1d8-0965b362b3fd", "value": "A spatially discrete group of pits usually containing artefactual material with little or no accompanying evidence for structural features."}
{"id": "20859d03-1c57-4afa-9fa5-13e410b30770", "value": "A pit for the reception of night-soil and refuse."}
{"id": "7ce529ec-90b9-4175-9a8c-63e79a0ab910", "value": "A pit dug in the ground used to store meat, grain and other foodstuffs. A common feature of Iron Age farms."}
{"id": "62f82746-1c91-4b42-8c78-9f8c52805d25", "value": "A pit where domestic waste material is deposited."}

{"id": "6ee045a2-5035-40d9-9eca-c5ae3ff39f1e", "value": "A pit lined with the bony cores of animal horns. Thought to date from the 17th/18th centuries and believed to have been used in the tanning industry although some may have been used for casting cannon."}
{"id": "219a4ccd-73c2-472c-93ce-c4ef218c2cf0", "value": "A pit where calcium oxide (Quicklime) has been hydrated to produce calcium hydroxide, known as slaked lime."}
{"id": "82a71e21-7d1b-41ba-a42a-6c89954f5887", "value": "A deep pit used for the burial of plague victims."}

{"id": "a19f028f-365a-4855-be74-d08bf7560b53", "value": "A pit dug into the ground or a simple construction made of stone, brick or metal. Designed to contain a fire and prevent it from spreading, but can also be used to heat stone for breaking."}
{"id": "5015bec6-8708-4081-af08-3a740ea126e9", "value": "A pit or enclosed area used for cockfighting."}

{"id": "a2451a97-1ef7-43d7-a7ab-3013780d8664", "value": "Surface workings including shallow shafts, lode workings, open-pit methods and quarrying including some mines of stone, clays, compounds, etc. See also MINERAL EXTRACTION SITE."}
{"id": "e8dd92eb-1443-40be-8934-d403a240b4a3", "value": "A pit where bears were housed for baiting and entertainment purposes. If not used for baiting use BEAR ENCLOSURE."}
{"id": "e93659ef-2131-4cb9-b8db-408a841275ba", "value": "Pit for soaking animal hides as part of the tanning process."}
{"id": "6a16f620-08b9-4354-b727-f2b4899b46c7", "value": "A pit or tank containing chemicals for the preserving of animal hide."}
{"id": "651e4a3f-625f-43e5-8ce6-7869e0f63063", "value": "A large, circular hollow, often with a platform and seating built into the sides, used for preaching."}
{"id": "cc1d0a65-6cd4-4d18-9ac8-c3bd311fc5d2", "value": "A pit dug for the extraction of brine."}
{"id": "6f224228-e32a-4183-9c7e-6b4815bee1e7", "value": "A pit or tank where the chemicals used in tanning are washed from the animal hides."}
{"id": "a3055434-5fcb-4943-9b8c-a17b3229e648", "value": "Pit for the depostion of ore sediment from waste water collected from ore washing."}
{"id": "a4032424-2eba-41da-8a26-aa483c8a9510", "value": "A hole or cavity in the ground, either natural or the result of excavation. Use more specific type where known."}
{"id": "3ee4fe69-7091-4909-89dd-d32d6968c67d", "value": "A pit containing burnt ashes."}

{"id": "5173ef4d-6341-4c77-9a5f-b90318cae4d7", "value": "An enclosure where the boundary consists of a line of discrete pits, as opposed to a continuous ditch. Use with a term that describes the shape of the monument."}
{"id": "17637567-bab5-43d9-a1f2-295a10bb1678", "value": "A hole dug in the ground to act as a, usually temporary, communal toilet facility."}
{"id": "651d7e3d-fb9e-40d1-a059-3fe1a8bcf5c1", "value": "The rectangular pit in which the lower part of a waterwheel revolves."}
{"id": "6c1a1c31-638b-49ea-84f3-fb01337dec75", "value": "A pit containing the waste product form iron working."}
{"id": "c6168c21-6eba-4fee-9481-bb9b350146fa", "value": "A place where tree trunks were sawn into planks by hand."}

{"id": "51d66fdb-4d87-41c6-b5cf-e9934fbe5dde", "value": "An airfield building housing a turret gunnery trainer used to teach air gunners how to report the correct position of enemy aircraft by practising shooting against projected moving images of enemy aircraft displayed on a target screen (WWII)."}

{"id": "fe0fc484-cec2-4d03-ae33-4283fdcffc8d", "value": "A dome shaped building, housing training apparatus, including a projector, for training ground gunners in the art of airfield defence. (WWII)."}
{"id": "83c2dafd-a4e7-492f-baa2-a68363ed616f", "value": "A pump used to transfer petrol from a storage tank into cars, lorries and other road vehicles."}
{"id": "e89746b5-e03f-43de-8291-ab4ac82c45d4", "value": "A building or room where motor vehicles are exhibited for sale."}
{"id": "ce2766cd-fd5d-41a5-8b40-3cbb582b1938", "value": "A place where vehicles can be filled up with petrol, oil, water, etc."}
{"id": "caffe761-b044-4607-b135-68f0d379153f", "value": "Use only for buildings which house motor vehicles. Includes garages for vehicle repair. For petrol sales use PETROL STATION."}
{"id": "0f5fd502-4ba9-43a3-9f1c-6660e941e575", "value": "An inclined concrete ramp on which cars can move from one level to another."}
{"id": "65a847fc-8d09-411a-8dc0-f459b302bc67", "value": "A car park, on two or more levels."}
{"id": "885cb156-91af-4302-838a-4aee42b50c69", "value": "A post to which ropes are attached to secure vessels at a landing place."}

{"id": "c97a0afd-d138-4e92-9916-725f6ba65c3c", "value": "A firm beach or foreshore used for landing and loading of ships and other vessels. In more recent times hards have been reinforced with concrete."}
{"id": "2ce01201-731f-4fb0-9093-0b37d409342e", "value": "A cluster of piles for mooring a vessel."}

{"id": "75afc459-f07f-4dbf-b469-225dedbf4e9d", "value": "Block, often made of concrete, to secure smaller maritime craft. Many were made during the Second Wold War to secure craft which were to be used in the D-Day landings."}

{"id": "d178dff3-2bdc-4152-aa75-3d0e10f8a04b", "value": "A section of the water channel of a river, shut off above and below by lock gates provided with sluices to let water in and out and thus raise or lower boats from one level to another. Often found situated next to a weir."}

{"id": "ff3d83be-9a60-4716-b120-598839abc979", "value": "A rectangular chamber of brick or stone with heavy wooden gates at either end equipped with sluices to let water in and out, thereby enabling a canal boat to be lowered or raised to a different level."}
{"id": "7b84c3fa-bba1-4f29-95e6-3f4febdb6f65", "value": "A gun battery used to signal warnings to ships during bad weather."}
{"id": "060f8c34-145c-4dd2-89c4-dfe1eac2ccb5", "value": "A signalling station which used a series of shutters to indicate various messages."}

{"id": "7b361f47-7a4f-4cc6-bd1a-a97b43811b2f", "value": "A building or tower used to communicate information to shipping or other stations using signals such as flags, fires or lights. Roman signal stations took the form of a stone tower surrounded by a ditched enclosure and were used to warn of Saxon raids."}

{"id": "ea119215-c73f-44ed-a816-f8aadb4e4b0a", "value": "A site or structure on which a signal, especially a fire, could be placed as a warning or means of communication. Use for beacon sites or surviving beacon structures."}

{"id": "494e62eb-5922-4511-9ca2-c61f8608390e", "value": "A tower in a semaphore communication system. Often a three-storey building on a hill in line-of-sight, signal towers provided working and living space, usually for two crewmen with their families."}
{"id": "b5abce45-e09f-4166-a012-dae14610956f", "value": "A structure with semaphore arms and/or coloured lights used as a means of warning on railway systems."}
{"id": "7796c5c9-2ebd-4403-b85f-37b3de8ee947", "value": "A bell mounted on an anchored vessel, buoy, headland, rock etc and rung as a warning to mariners in foggy weather."}

{"id": "cae883e0-06e3-4ca0-a882-9ade42870df8", "value": "A tower or structure, with a powerful light or lights at the top, usually erected at an important or dangerous point on or near the sea-coast for the warning and guidance of mariners, but can also be erected inland for the guidance of travellers."}

{"id": "46a992f8-4d46-4f14-b36a-2415f7c6440f", "value": "A building on a railway system housing levers used to regulate trains on the tracks using signals and to change the points to enable a train to transfer from one track to another."}
{"id": "208c7500-7059-40f8-b922-e213a020d12d", "value": "A steam whistle or siren used for signalling purposes."}

{"id": "9eaf9831-b6c9-48cb-8894-e822ac709214", "value": "A cast iron post similar to a lamp post, with revolving top to carry either coloured plates, or an oil lamp with coloured glass at night. Associated with canal or river navigation locks."}
{"id": "783f09b5-a4ba-4b11-bbcd-aeb334d12a09", "value": "Buildings and structures associated with signal communication."}

{"id": "6851f6e0-b8c4-4139-8d46-c67dc54c2e9d", "value": "A signalling structure used on WWII airfields, comprising a concrete square base with a kerbed border into which concrete signal symbols could be placed to advise pilots in the air of current airfield state e.g. directions of landing and airfield circuit."}
{"id": "b674a1a6-3046-427e-b6e5-07c4fb6ffd44", "value": "An instrument used for making a loud sound for information or warning."}
{"id": "b068d2f5-7d6d-417f-91fa-fef55c0d9564", "value": "A structure found on lighthouses, piers, etc, capable of emitting a loud noise to warn shipping in foggy weather."}
{"id": "d81b0f83-4bc3-4013-bb8f-c59b25cc9fb0", "value": "A signal station incorporating equipment for visually conveying coded communications."}

{"id": "b7fba4c8-02d9-4a4f-a4a4-2ec06892a4a6", "value": "Large concrete letters representing the ground-to-air airfield code. It has been used to show pilots in WWII the name of the airfield they were above e.g. DW for Dunkeswell."}
{"id": "eaf53d57-887b-4cc4-82d1-eaed1b21f59d", "value": "A factory producing drabbet, a type of linen cloth."}
{"id": "ef5b4320-0e65-41b2-b631-8545a4fe2b7a", "value": "A mill where flax fibres were woven into linen cloth."}
{"id": "5b7edd03-5226-4ddc-be43-7f1848c2c880", "value": "A mill where flax is processed to make linen, thread and yarn."}
{"id": "9c1cac4a-1058-4592-89f3-800833d45f11", "value": "Finishing process for cloth, especially linen, running the cloth between heavy rollers."}
{"id": "e07f26ca-8d04-4159-bc05-6869dd174309", "value": "A finishing process for cloth involving the pounding of the cloth with heavy weights."}
{"id": "1196b426-298f-4674-8513-56a3594c242c", "value": "A school associated with a cathedral or college originally intended to provide a general education for their choristers."}
{"id": "eea15968-09cd-4ed6-92c6-20cb28768b8f", "value": "The principal church of a diocese in which the cathedra or bishop's throne is to be found."}
{"id": "b71c8337-29e3-45b4-afbf-a717ac635fa9", "value": "A residence for all clergy having the sole or subordinate charge of a living."}

{"id": "0119e060-b3ed-429a-9006-ce51a3483baa", "value": "A tall building, either round, square or polygonal in plan, used for a variety of purposes, including defence, as a landmark, for the hanging of bells, industrial functions, etc. Use more specific type where known."}

{"id": "6dec363f-0cca-48cb-a6fd-c50dff59089e", "value": "A structure used for the production of hydraulic power. A head of water was raised at the top of the tower by means of pumps. Used for powering machinery."}

{"id": "7b7fefca-f796-4533-a5e6-d1ff5f54b49c", "value": "A place of worship for Unitarians, a movement which does not believe in the Trinity but only in the Unity of Christ. Christ was to them just an exalted human teacher."}
{"id": "b7f14cfd-3add-427c-be52-2da4824b6599", "value": "A place of worship for members of Protestant sects dissenting from the established Church."}

{"id": "f9c73614-cdcf-41c0-95de-2450bf66c2eb", "value": "A place of worship for the sect known as 'Cokelers', formed circa 1850 by John Sirgood. Most aspects of Dependent belief are fairly orthodox within the Arminian traditions of Protestant dissent. Chapels can be found in Sussex, Surrey, London and Kent."}

{"id": "c8259c3e-80c0-4990-a67c-b22bfe215eef", "value": "A place of worship for followers of Emmanuel Swedenborg who believed he was the medium through which the New Jerusalem would be founded on earth. The church was formed in 1787."}
{"id": "3662c20d-d100-4acb-8254-3bbd67a0e4f0", "value": "A place of worship for Methodists, a movement founded by John Wesley. Following his death in 1791 there were many secessions."}
{"id": "a83e201b-0e1c-429a-ad45-f9417c4538da", "value": "A place of worship for Baptists. The first Baptist church was formed by Thomas Helws in 1611 and gave rise to the General Baptist Movement."}

{"id": "d6dbfc0d-f41b-4f60-b18d-aa22030b4f05", "value": "A place of worship for Presbyterians, a movement who started off attempting to reform Anglicanism before breaking away in 1660. Sometimes referred to as moderate puritans, they joined with the Congregationalists to form the United Reformed church in 1972."}
{"id": "809fb308-d983-4f9b-b9a8-c43fd39eeb1d", "value": "A place of worship for members of Protestant sects dissenting from the established Church."}
{"id": "7ed2d48f-5e2c-4776-afd3-e1285ac7575d", "value": "A place of worship for Protestant followers of Hussite doctrines which accept the Bible as the only source of faith."}

{"id": "b1d11213-ebc2-41be-9fd7-2863db7e5699", "value": "A place of worship for members of the Congregational Church. These churches, the first of which was founded in 1616 in Southwark, practised self government. Most of them were merged to form the United Reformed Church in 1972."}
{"id": "7878b45c-f461-4662-8fb2-4394b91fac5f", "value": "A chapel for followers of Benjamin Ingham after he left the Moravians prior to joining the Sandamanians."}
{"id": "482d3550-8359-47da-9e09-297bdc07ce80", "value": "A building used for services by a nonconformist protestant sect, especially by Quakers and Presbyterians."}

{"id": "8b3f40bd-3a1d-4bb5-8e55-4aebaeccf840", "value": "A place of worship for Sandemanians, a movement founded by John Glass after his expulsion from the Church of Scotland in 1728. It was spread to England by his son-in-law, Robert Sandeman."}

{"id": "3d2348bd-f36c-4cbc-9ed1-44434e9868e8", "value": "A place of worship for Christadelphians, a fundamentalist sect founded in America in the late 1840s who rejected the trinity and awaited the second coming of Christ."}

{"id": "daa23c25-23ee-4bdd-94b4-c2f6b3539a45", "value": "A building within a gunpowder works complex, where the mill cake (pulverised and incorporated ingredients of gunpowder) was broken down. It was crushed or broken down by passing it between pairs of revolving gunmetal rollers in a breaking-down machine."}

{"id": "92008354-cff5-4bb9-a907-41813516132b", "value": "A building within the gunpowder works complex. During the gunpowder production process, the mill cake was broken down, pressed and then corned. The remaining dust was removed from the corned powder by tumbling it in gauze-covered revolving cylinders."}
{"id": "3480c126-3056-4bff-b9e1-72d9c34e79d1", "value": "An official residence of a bishop used during the summer months."}
{"id": "e190b13f-730e-45de-b35f-60c6a1f1437f", "value": "An official residence of an abbot during the summer months."}
{"id": "a5cb0dec-3d11-48a6-8b9a-3638bd38dcce", "value": "A site used by the Air Raid Precautions network. Use more specific term."}
{"id": "70d52b91-4956-439c-b819-cbf88b1d52d6", "value": "A building used for the storage and distribution of civilian respirators and Air Raid Precautions equipment."}

{"id": "bb790369-3633-40e9-abbd-fb9748f660b5", "value": "A building or structure used to provide protection to an Air Raid Warden or firewatcher during an air raid, thus enabling the identification of the locations of fires caused by incendiary bombs in comparative safety."}

{"id": "9e020fe6-eaf3-4dab-a0a0-1fe8dcb814bb", "value": "A building used as a control centre for the Air Raid Precautions network, responsible for issuing air raid warnings and coordinating fire and rescue services."}
{"id": "d48b9dc5-9852-483f-ba0d-dc687dcb3a10", "value": "A centre used by the Air Raid Precautions network to co-ordinate reports of air raids in an area."}

{"id": "5de56cf2-d4a3-40f8-9e66-94af52910e77", "value": "A brick built railway signal box, usually with a reinforced correct roof, designed to minimize the effects of blast damage from aerial bombardment and thus protect the signalling equipment."}
